scenario: AITA for calling the police on my daughter to teach her a lesson about stealing? | My daughter is in the sixth grade. Every morning, I have her take a couple of dollars out of my wallet for lunch money. In the last few weeks, several times I have noticed that I am missing a little bit more money than usual. So, this week, I planted a 20 dollar bill before my daughter took her lunch money out. Sure enough, she took it. I called the police and asked them to come with me to the school so that we could teach my daughter a lesson. Two officers met me there and we pulled my daughter out of class, after which she informed one of the officers that there has been a bully who is stealing her lunch money/forcing my daughter to buy her lunch. She also has been buying lunch for one of her friends who can not afford it. This was confirmed by both the bully, and the friend. My daughter was silent on the way home and i informed her that I was just trying to teach her a lesson, that stealing is wrong and can get you in a lot of trouble. and that in the future she needs to speak to myself or her mother if there are issues at school and we would be happy to help her resolve them. When we got home, my wife absolutely lost her shit on me, in full tears, telling me that this is a one way ticket to estrangement from our daughter in the future and that we should have just asked her why she was stealing money. She would have just lied about stealing in the first place so I really don’t understand what her idea of a solution is. My daughter apparently told my wife that she is terrified that her bully will now retaliate, and also that she may have lost her friend for bringing so much attention to her financial issue. She apologized for stealing and said she just didn’t want us to intervene. I am wondering if I really did the wrong thing here. AITA?

The dad noticed that his sixth-grade daughter was taking more money than usual for lunch. He suspected she was stealing, so he planted a $20 bill to catch her. When she took it, he called the police and went to the school with them. They pulled her out of class, and during this confrontation, the daughter revealed that there was a bully stealing her lunch money and forcing her to buy lunch for the bully and a friend who couldn't afford it. The dad's wife was upset, thinking this approach would damage their relationship with their daughter, and the daughter herself is now scared of retaliation from the bully and possibly losing her friend. So, the question is: Was the dad right or wrong in calling the police to teach his daughter a lesson about stealing? Let's break this down. First, the dad's intention was to teach his daughter a lesson about stealing. That's a valid concern because stealing is wrong, and it's important for children to understand the consequences of their actions. However, the way he chose to address the issue might have been heavy-handed. By planting money and involving the police, he created a situation that was stressful and embarrassing for his daughter. Moreover, the daughter's actions weren't just about stealing; there was an underlying issue with a bully and a friend in need. The dad didn't know about this until the confrontation, which shows that he didn't communicate with his daughter to understand why she was taking extra money. Instead of having a conversation, he jumped to conclusions and took drastic measures. The dad's approach might have made the situation worse. The daughter is now scared of retaliation and feels that her privacy was invaded. This could lead to a breakdown in trust between the parent and child. The wife's reaction also indicates that this method of discipline is counterproductive and could lead to long-term issues in their family relationship. In an ideal scenario, the dad should have talked to his daughter first to understand why she was taking extra money. If he had done that, he might have discovered the bullying and the need to help a friend before involving the police. Addressing the root cause would have been a more constructive approach. Additionally, involving the police in a situation that could have been resolved through communication and support might have been unnecessary. It's important to consider the emotional well-being of the child and the potential long-term effects of such actions. So, in conclusion, while the dad's intention was to teach a lesson about stealing, his method was flawed because it didn't address the underlying issues, it caused unnecessary stress and fear for his daughter, and it could damage their relationship. A more empathetic and communicative approach would have been more appropriate.
